The charge sheet has been filed in this case by the Police Inspector of North Women police station against the accused no.1 to 3 for the alleged offences punishable under Sections 498A r/w Sec. 34 of IPC and Sec. 3 and 4 of D.P.Act.

sentences.text:
In briefly the case of the prosecution is as follows:-
It is the case of the prosecution that the accused no.1 married C.W.1- P.Darshini on 21.01.2024 at Ayyappa Community Hall, Pipeline road, T.Dasarahalli, at Bengaluru and the accused No.1 to 3 with an intention to commit an offence and in furtherance of their common intention demanded the parents of C.W1 to buy the accused no.1 a Royal Enfield motorcycle, 05 soverign gold, one KG silver, cash of Rs.5,00,000/- and Rs.50,000/- for buying clothes, household articles like almirah, cot, bed, blanket and at the time of marriage the accused no.1 to 3 received Royal Enfield motorcycle, 05 soverign gold, one KG silver, cash of Rs.5,00,000/- and Rs.50,000/- for buying clothes, household articles like almirah, cot, bed, blanket.

Further, after marriage while C.W.1 was residing with the accused no.1 to 3 at the matrimonial home, the accused no.1 to 3 ill treated C.W.1 and harassed her, extended physical and mental torture towards C.W.1 by demanding additional dowry in form of 05 soverign gold,
therefore the C.W.1 lodged the complaint against accused before the Basavanagudi Women Police seeking necessary action against them in accordance with law.
3. On the basis of the said complaint given by C.W.1, the complainant police have registered the case under Crime No.69/2024 and sent FIR to this Court and to their concerned higher authorities.

Thereafter, the complainant police have visited the spot and conducted the spot C.C.9237/2025 mahazar in the presence of the panch witnesses, herein after recorded the statements of witnesses who availed in the station subsequently who availed where the said mahazars have been drawn,
after completion of the investigation the IO has arived at a conclusion that there are sufficient materials as to prosecute the accused, for which charge sheet has been filed for the above said offences.

4. After filing of the charge sheet, this Court registered the case is as numbered above, subsequently the accused no.1 to 3 obtained anticipatory bail and in persuance of summons the accused appeared before this Court and was enlarged on bail, meanwhile copies of the charge sheet and other prosecution papers were duly supplied as required under Section 207 of Cr.P.C.

After hearing both sides, this court found that there were sufficient reasons so as to frame charge against the accused ,
therefore charge was framed and read over and explained to the accused no.1 to 3 in the language known to them, after understanding the same they denied the same and claimed to be tried,
accordingly, proceeded with trial.
5. In order to prove its case, the prosecution has examined one witness who is said to be victim as P.W.1 and got marked three documents at Ex.P-1 to P.3.

As there are no any incriminating materials forth coming against the accused, as to which summoning of remaining witnesses would no purpose to serve and therefore CW-2 to 8 ordered to be given up by rejecting the submission made by the learned PP.
Consequently, recording of statement of accused as required under section 313 of Cr.P.C also dispensed with.

6. Heard both side arguments, in compliance of section 437-A of Cr.P.C., bail bond were obtained from the accused.

sentences.text:
In view of above said facts and circumstances the following points that would arise for my consideration are as follows:-
POINTS FOR CONSIDERATION 1.

Whether the prosecution further proves beyond all reasonable doubt that the accused no.1 married C.W.1-P.Darshini on 21.01.2024 at Ayyappa Community Hall,
Pipeline road, T.Dasarahalli, at Bengaluru and the accused No.1 to 3 with an intention to commit an offence and in furtherance of their common intention demanded the parents of C.W1 to buy the accused no.1 a Royal Enfield motorcycle, 05 soverign gold, one KG silver, cash of Rs.5,00,000/- and Rs.50,000/- for buying clothes, household articles like almirah, cot, bed, blanket as dowry and thereby the accused has committed an offence punishable under section 3 of D.P. Act?

2. Whether the prosecution proves beyond all reasonable doubt that after marriage while C.W.1 was residing with the accused no.1 to 3 at the matrimonial home, the accused no.1 to 3 ill treated C.W.1 and harassed her, extended physical and mental torture towards C.W.1 by demanding additional dowry in form of 05 soverign gold and thereby the accused have subjected C.W.1 to cruelty and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 498A r/w Sec. 34 of IPC?

3. Whether the prosecution further proves beyond all reasonable doubt that accused with an intention to get additional dowry demanded C.W.1 to get additional dowry in the form of 05 soverign gold ornaments and received a Royal Enfield motorcycle, 05 soverign gold, one KG silver, cash of Rs.5,00,000/- and Rs.50,000/- for buying clothes, household articles like almirah, C.C.9237/2025 cot, bed, blanket as dowry and thereby the accused have committed the offence punishable under section 4 of D.P.Act?
4. What Order?

8. My answers to the above points are as under:
Point Nos.1 to 3 : In the 'Negative' Point No.4 : As per the final order, for the following:-
REASONS 9. Point No.1 to3 : These points are taken up together for common discussion in order to avoid the repetation of facts.
North Women Police Station vs Sudeesh S on 1 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/160335109/
3 10.

In order to prove its case, the prosecution has examined the complainant/C.W.1 as P.W.1 and got marked two documents on her behalf as Ex.P.1 and P.2 as far as appreciation of oral and documentary evidence is concerned P.W.1 is the complainant by name Darshini and she deposed in her evidence that accused no.1 is her ex husband and her marriage was solemnized with the accused no.1 on 21.01.2024.

Further she deposed that after her marriage with the accused no.1 she was residing at the matrimonial house with the accused no.1 to 3 and they were living with together in cordial terms and the accused persons did not extend any physical and mental harassment towards her by demanding additional dowry and the accused did not demand any dowry in the form of Royal Enfield bike, gold and silver article and Cash.
She further deposed that she has not lodged complaint against the accused persons.

She deposed that when she had been to North Women PS in the year 2024, police took her signatures on two documents and she does not know the contents of Ex.P.1 and P.2 and police did not draw any mahazar before her presence as per Ex.P.2.

She identified her signature on Ex.P.1 and Ex.P.2 but she pleaded ignorance about the C.C.9237/2025 contents of Ex.P-1 and 2 as to which when learned Assistant Public Prosecutor treated this witness as hostile and with the permission of the court, cross-examined her even in that process also learned A.P.P.
failed to elicit anything from her mouth.

11. As the first informant/complainant P.W.1 being the material witness in this case has not supported the case of the prosecution and as she turned hostile by giving a complete go-bye statement, due to which other prosecution witness were given up, as it would serve no purpose to summon the other witnesses, during the course of prosecution evidence Three documents got marked as Ex.P1 to P.3.

So far as Ex.P1 is the complaint, Ex.P.2 is the spot mahazar, but the prosecution witness did not support the contents which are mentioned in the same, therefore whatever the suspicious circumstances pleaded while framing of charge remained as same.

On considering these facts herein no incriminating materials forthcoming against the accused persons and the prosecution has not established the ingredients of the alleged offences against the accused however herein no positive evidence to prove the guilt of the accused, for which this Court is of the considered opinion that prosecution has failed to prove the guilt of the accused beyond all reasonable doubt.
Hence, benefit of doubt goes to the accused, for which I answer point Nos.1 to 4 in the 'Negative'.
12. Point No.5:

In view of my findings on point Nos.1 to 4 and reasons assigned therein, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER

Acting under Section 248(1) of Cr.P.C., the accused no.1 to 3 are not found guilty and they are hereby acquitted of the offences punishable C.C.9237/2025 under Secs.498A r/w Sec. 34 of IPC and Sec.3 and 4 of D.P.Act.
The bail bond executed by the accused No.1 to 3 stands cancelled.

In compliance of section 437-A of Cr.P.C. the bail bond executed by the accused no.1 to 3 is ordered to be continued in force for six months or till issuance of notice in respect of any appeal [if preferred] against the present Judgment before the Appellate Court.
